Seminar Title:

Deep Learning based Abdominal Multi-Organ and Kidney Disease Segmentation from CT Images

Seminar Type:

Synopsis Seminar

Department:

Computer Science and Engineering

Speaker Name:

Santoshi Gorli ( Rollno : 521cs8014)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Convention Hall, CSE Department

Date and Time:

13 Oct 2026 12:15 PM

Contact:

Ratnakar Dash

Abstract:

Accurate segmentation of abdominal organs and diseases from Computed Tomography (CT) images is important for computer-aided diagnosis, treatment planning, disease assessment and quantitative analysis. However, automatic segmentation is challenging due to low tissue contrast, high anatomical variability, class imbalance, small pathological regions, irregular boundaries, and large variations in organ appearance. These challenges are exacerbated when segmentation models need to operate with limited computational resources or in real-time clinical settings. To tackle these challenges, this work proposes a progressive deep learning framework for accurate, boundary-aware, computationally efficient and semantically guided abdominal CT segmentation.The first contribution introduces a Trans-Kronecker contextual-enriched U-Net, where the proposed Kronecker convolution increases the effective receptive field with lower complexity than conventional dilated convolution. The integration of Swin Transformer-based encoding and decoding improves contextual representation and enables effective segmentation of abdominal organs and kidney-related abnormalities. The model achieves consistent and robust segmentation accuracy across multi-organ, Kidney Tumor and Kidney Stone dataset. The model also demonstrates improved detection of small tumor regions in the KiTS19 dataset, although precise boundary delineation remains challenging. The second contribution addresses this limitation through a fusion loss and superpixel-guided loss. The fusion loss combines Focal and Dice losses to improve pixel classification and handle region imbalance, while the superpixel-guided loss introduces structural constraints for improved spatial consistency and boundary preservation. Compared with the Trans-Kronecker baseline, the proposed approach reduces mHD by 0.88, 0.58, and 0.89 across the evaluated datasets, demonstrating improved boundary localization. The third contribution focuses on computational efficiency and real-time deployment through a ViT-based slice-filtering mechanism integrated with MLite. The framework reduces unnecessary processing of non-informative CT slices while maintaining segmentation performance, memory efficiency, and low inference latency, thereby providing a foundation for Edge-AI-based real-time kidney disease segmentation. The fourth contribution further enhances structural representation through an Edge-aware Graph Convolution Fusion (EGCF) framework with superpixel-guided learning. The approach strengthens local boundary and structural information using graph convolution. However, the graph convolution &nbspincreases computational overhead.&nbsp The semantic ambiguities in low-contrast and small pathological regions motivate the development of more computationally efficient and semantically guided segmentation. The fifth contribution introduces a prompt-guided segmentation framework integrating CLIP, EGCF, Channel-Aware Bidirectional Cross-Fusion (CA-BiCF), and Hypernetwork-driven Iterative Mask Optimization (HIMO). The framework incorporates high-level semantic guidance while replacing the computationally expensive SAM image encoder with a lightweight Trans-Kronecker encoder. The combined approach achieves 85.45\% mDSC with only 6.85 GFLOPs.
Overall, the developed frameworks demonstrate that combining contextual, structural, computational, and semantic information can improve the reliability and efficiency of abdominal CT segmentation.
